title: Moto Phase 6 — scenes and continuity (moto-scenes-v2)
description: One answer of Phase 6 for a custom motorcycle film: the approved beats grouped into scenes, with the blocking of people and things, the continuity each scene starts and ends with, its incoming transition and the work its beats show on parts. A scene has no screen time: the shot plan sets it. Environment assignments, events, characters, configurations and motorcycle states stay with the beats and are derived by code.

flags.description: Short notes for the reviewer. With status partial, name briefly what blocks, including a blocking conflict carried from the background text, without copying whole conflicts. With status fail, name the fault in the input.

evidence.description: Evidence paths resolve against this Phase 6 input; do not copy another phase's internal evidence paths unchanged or rewrite them by adding a prefix. path: dot-separated keys starting at a top-level key of this input; a list item is named by its id, by its beat or by its zero-based index, e.g. script.beats.B4.link, locations.beats.B11.uses.0.background, design_states.states.BS07.previously_present. A conflict of the background text is cited through its record kept in this input, e.g. locations.conflicts.0.note. quote: text copied verbatim from a text field or an item of a text list. value: the exact value and type of an id, an enumerated value, a number, a boolean, null or structured data; ids and enumerated values are never quoted.

detached_part.description: A part off the motorcycle at the scene's build state, read from that state in design_states.states, or held off by the scene's work: then being_made while the state lists it in progress, removed when it was on before, otherwise awaiting_install. Without work, being_made: listed in its in_progress. awaiting_install: a finished part waiting to be fitted, listed in both its previously_in_progress (by the workflow's convention, work an earlier state does and this one no longer does is finished; this is no proof) and its installed_later; for a part not listed in both, leave detached_parts null or record a conflict. removed: listed in its previously_present.

protection.description: One character present at that moment. items: null when the character's equipment is unknown, [] when it is established that they wear none, otherwise what they wear for their action, a visor only when their helmet has one.

character.description: The id of a character of script.characters.

continuity.description: The staging state at the start or end of the scene beyond the source records. Use null only where the schema allows it; keep every required key. null marks an unestablished or inapplicable detail, [] an established absence. detached_parts and lights_on are null in a scene without a physical build state (BS06–BS12). Protection is always an array; use items: null for a character whose equipment is unknown.

lights_on.description: Ids from design_states.lights that are on, each on a part present at the scene's build state and installed and operable no later than that state.

protection.description: The characters present at that moment, each once; [] when no character needs a record then, never to hide what is unknown. A character may enter or leave within the scene.

transition.description: A match_cut cites the link, visual or sfx of the last beat before the scene or of its first beat. A time_jump cites the time_jump value, other than none, of one of those two beats.

work_item.description: What is done to a part in one beat of the scene and where it is at the start and the end of that work, in beat order. with: the parts worked together with it, sharing its place; parts mounted on a part go with it. make only while the build state lists the part in progress; finish, assemble and paint keep it where it is; test_fit puts on, to try it, a part that has not been on the motorcycle; remove takes off a part that is on; reinstall puts back one that was on before, by its first_state or by earlier work; install puts on for the first time a part the build state has present. A part the build state lists only in progress is being_made wherever it is: it starts off the motorcycle until work of that build state puts it on, may be tried on, taken off and put back, and is never installed; its first test_fit counts as having been on, so it goes back on with reinstall. Within a build state a part starts where its last work left it; at a finished state every part ends on. Evidence comes from the beat: paths under script.beats.<beat>.

purpose.description: One sentence on what the scene does in the story; never a rewrite of its beats.

set_brief.description: The arrangement of the place the scene needs beyond the background records, as staging notes; never a repeat of the background or a render prompt; null when nothing is needed.

blocking.description: Where each person and each thing stands at the start of the scene and how they move through its events: who works and who watches, from which side a person or a part comes in, which hand or tool meets which part, and the jig, stand or support that holds the motorcycle or the part. People are named by character id, parts by part id. Staging only: no camera, no lens, no timing.

conflict.description: Names what it affects: at least one scene or beat; when it names scenes, every beat it names lies in one of them. A conflict about a beat that cannot fit the grouping rules, such as a beat assigned to more than one place, blocks.
